name: AMD Instinct MI325X
memory_bandwidth_basis: 'Up to 6 TB/s' per the AMD spec table. Same 8192-bit interface as MI300X but HBM3E at a higher data rate (spec table 'Memory Clock 6 GHz'). AMD footnote MI325-001A gives 6 TB/s as an AMD Performance Labs calculation from 2024-09-26 'based on current specifications and/or estimation', so read it as ~6.0 TB/s theoretical, not measured.
notes:
MI300X with more and faster memory, nothing else. Identical compute silicon: 304 CUs, 1216 matrix cores, 19,456 SPs, 2100 MHz, 153B transistors, same 8192-bit interface. The only changes are 256 GB HBM3E instead of 192 GB HBM3, 6 TB/s instead of 5.3 TB/s, and 1000W instead of 750W TBP.

Same eight-XCD caveat as MI300X: 256 GB is one package-level address space across 8 compute dies, not two devices.

Because the compute flops are identical to MI300X, ANY benchmark gap between the two parts is a pure memory capacity/bandwidth effect. This is the capacity sweet spot of the CDNA3 generation: 256 GB per OAM at 1000W, versus MI300X's 192 GB at 750W.

ROCm LLVM target gfx942, identical to MI300X. 54V UBB, passive OAM, 8 Infinity Fabric links at 128 GB/s.
